text: Appendix ATest MetricsTo assess CV performances of the segmentation method, we used the following metrics: –Dice score: it is a measure of volumetric overlap between two structures A and B, defined as 2vA∩BvA+vB where v⋅ represents the volume of a structure.–Intersection over union: it is a measure of volumetric overlap between two structures A and B, defined as vA∩BvA∪B where v⋅ represents the volume of a structure.–True positive rate: it is defined as TP/(TP + FN), where TP = number of true positives, FN = number of false negatives, FP = number of false positives.–False discovery rate: it is defined as FP/(FP + TP), where TP = number of true positives, FN = number of false negatives, FP = number of false positives.–Robust Hausdorff distance: we used Hausdorff distance (Huttenlocher et al. 1993) with 95% percentile.–Mean surface distance: mean surface distance between two surfaces S and S′ is defined as 1nS+nS′∑p∈Sdp,S′+∑p′∈S′dp′S where nS,nS′ are the number of points on surfaces S and S′ respectively, and for a given point p∈S we define the distance from S′ as dp,S′=minp′∈S′∥p−p′∥2.–Volumetric similarity: volumetric similarity between two structures A and B is defined as 1−∣vA−vB∣vA+vB where v⋅ represents the volume of a structure.

Appendix BIncreasing the Robustness of the Method by Adding Voxel‐Wise NoiseWe compared the model with and without adding random voxel‐wise Gaussian noise in the synthetic intensity images during training. The noise is added as part of the intensity image augmentation right after the bias field simulation, in the following way: We sample a standard deviation σ from a uniform distribution σ∈U0,100, then sample independent voxel‐wise Gaussian noise from N0σ2, and add it to the intensity image with probability 95%.For the case with noise, we used the model trained on the first fold of the CV described in Section 3.3, following the same procedure for selecting the best epoch (i.e., maximizing the Dice score on the validation set of that fold). We then applied the resulting model to all IXI subjects and computed the QC score as detailed in Section 3.4. We then trained a model on the same CV fold without adding noise to the synthetic images, and repeated the same procedure. We obtained an average QC score on the IXI dataset of 0.555 ± 0.050 for the model with noise, and 0.490 ± 0.094 for the one without noise, which compare to the average QC metric on the manual labels of 0.539 ± 0.078, showing that the model with noise achieves more robust results.
